title: Wear a mask and limit time outdoors during dusty harmattan days
summary: Ghana Health Service advice for dusty, dry weather: limit outdoor activity, wear a face mask, drink water and keep taking asthma medicine.
details: Limit outdoor activities.
Wear a face mask.
Stay hydrated.
People with asthma or other chronic respiratory conditions should keep taking their medication.

sources.title: Graphic Online: See the 4 measures the Ghana Health Service has prescribed amid harsh weather conditions

title: Report open waste burning to your assembly
summary: A clean air campaign with 13 Accra assemblies says residents can report open waste burning by phone so the assembly can act.
details: The campaign is run by Infinity 970 with Breathe Cities Accra and the Clean Air Fund.
It works with 13 municipal assemblies in Accra, including Ayawaso North.

sources.title: MyJoyOnline: Accra residents urged to report open waste burning (10 Sep 2026)

title: Use Breathe Accra's neighbourhood air sensors
summary: Breathe Cities has put 67 real-time air quality sensors across 13 Accra districts.
details: 67 low-cost sensors across 13 districts.
Data goes to municipal assemblies to guide action on waste burning.

verification.flag_reason: Spot check failed: the page says the data is public but gives no link or app where residents can see it.

title: Plant and care for a tree through Tree for Life
summary: Ghana's Tree for Life initiative aims to plant 30 million seedlings in 2026. Trees cool streets and homes.
details: Launched 19 March 2026 at Achimota Forest Reserve.
30 million seedlings targeted for 2026.

sources.title: Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources: Ghana launches Tree for Life initiative

title: Send waste to the Accra Compost and Recycling Plant
summary: The Integrated Recycling and Compost Plant on Mortuary Road recycles and composts solid waste from central Accra communities.
details: Capacity of 400 tonnes per 16-hour shift, with an 80% recovery rate.
Located on Mortuary Road, set up to serve communities including Korle Bu, Chorkor, James Town and Agbogbloshie.

sources.title: Accra Metropolitan Assembly: Clean Accra Agenda: Integrated Recycling and Compost Plant commissioned

verification.flag_reason: Freshness check failed: the only official source is from April 2019, and it doesn't say whether residents can bring waste there directly.

title: Stay away from drains and flooded roads in heavy rain
summary: GMet advises moving away from flood-prone areas when warned, avoiding open drains, not driving through flooded roads and not dumping refuse in drains.
details: Relocate from flood-prone areas when warnings are issued.
Avoid open drains during heavy rain.
Don't drive through flooded roads.
Don't dump refuse into drains.

title: Get your plastic waste picked up for recycling
summary: Coliba collects plastic, paper and drink cans for recycling across Accra. You can request a pickup or use one of its recycling hubs.
details: Request a pickup with the online waste pickup form or by calling 0200028851.
Coliba says it has over 40 recycling centres and hubs across Accra.
The Coliba 2.0 app shows the nearest collection point.
Collected plastic is turned into flakes and pellets for new products.
